name: Diplomatic and consular post records
one_line: J-DEPTH placeholder template for the working file of a diplomatic mission or consular post: an authority of a sending state operating on the territory of a host state, reporting back to its own capital, transacting with the host government, and providing protection and documentary services to its nationals abroad. It is not activated by an embassy name, a coat of arms, diplomatic vocabulary, a handling caption, a country pair, or by holding a visa, passport, or legalisation the post issued. Its distinct default is the post/sending-state/host-state role triangle, a purpose-coherent but content-incoherent post drawer, and an extraterritorial privacy posture in which named nationals sit inside a foreign jurisdiction. It declares no fields and no dimensions under PR-6.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every signal below is template-activation evidence on the fieldless `government` schema, never a licence to write a post, mission, country, national, case, or classification fact. The holder or producer must be evidenced on the post's own side of the mission, not as an applicant to it, a visitor of it, a citizen of it, or a reader of what it published.

a reporting despatch or telegram-shaped report carrying an explicit origin-post block and an addressed capital or desk (a from-post / to-ministry pair), plus a subject line, numbered or captioned paragraphs, a distribution or copy list, and a post reference number

a note verbale or third-person diplomatic note: mission letterhead, an outgoing note number, an addressee that is a host-state foreign ministry or protocol department, third-person 'presents its compliments' construction, a seal rather than a personal signature, and often a reciprocal incoming note number quoted

a demarche or instruction-and-delivery pair: an instruction addressed from capital to post naming talking points or a text to be delivered, matched to a delivery or readout record naming the host-state interlocutor and the date of delivery

a protocol or accreditation register produced by or for the post: staff names with diplomatic ranks, accreditation and agrément dates, identity-card or accreditation numbers, dependants, and privileges or immunities status

a consular protection or assistance case file held by the post: an internal case reference, a named national, a host-state authority (police, prison, hospital, morgue, court), a notification or consular-access date, a visit or welfare log, and next-of-kin or emergency-contact slots

a post-side documentary-services record: passport or emergency-travel-document issuance registers, notarial and legalisation act books, apostille registers, or consular reports of birth, marriage, or death abroad, each showing the issuing-side slots (act number, officer, fee taken) rather than only the holder's copy

a post-side visa or entry-permission adjudication record: an application or case number tied to interview notes, eligibility findings, refusal reasons under a named provision, and an adjudicating-officer marker

a crisis, evacuation, or travel-advice operations record scoped to a named host state or region: warden or contact networks, assembly points, evacuation phases, incident logs, or advice-change records held by the post rather than read by a traveller

a treaty or instrument action held on the negotiating or depositary side: exchange-of-letters pairs, signature or ratification instruments, depositary notifications, full-powers documents, or an internal negotiating record naming both delegations

post administration bound to the mission itself: post estate and residence records, locally engaged staff terms, mission security and guard arrangements, consular fee reconciliation, or diplomatic bag and courier records
an authority export, registry transfer, or archive manifest whose members are coherently post-produced across several of the families above and that names a post as the producing unit
needs_llm: deciding whether a report is post-produced field reporting addressed upward to a capital, or a capital-produced policy or country paper that merely cites a post; the discriminator is an origin-post block plus an addressed desk, not the presence of country analysis

deciding whether a named-person case is consular protection abroad or domestic constituent or social-services casework; the discriminator is a host-state authority and an extraterritorial national, not the fact that a public office holds a person's case

deciding whether a passport, visa, legalisation, apostille, or civil-registration document sits on the issuing side or the holder side; the discriminator is an issuing register, act book, officer marker, or adjudication reasoning versus a single finished document bearing the holder's own name
deciding whether a bilateral cooperation or aid record is mission representation work or programme administration of a development portfolio
deciding whether procurement, payroll, estate, or security records belong to the post as an authority unit or to an ordinary organisation with an international office
reading a handling caption, distribution marking, or release instruction as a literal source observation rather than as a sensitivity taxonomy the product may adopt
deciding whether an archive or registry export is a post transfer to a records authority or an already-accessioned archival holding
never_alone: an embassy, consulate, high commission, permanent mission, foreign ministry, ambassador, consul, attache, or chancery name alone; the post may be issuer, host, employer, counterparty, venue, or the subject of a news article
a coat of arms, national flag pair, mission letterhead, seal, wax stamp, or an official-looking bilingual header alone

diplomatic and international vocabulary alone: demarche, note verbale, aide-memoire, bilateral, multilateral, protocol, accreditation, credentials, treaty, ratification, consular. Advocacy organisations, international-relations research, model-UN material, journalism, and law teaching use the identical register

a handling or distribution caption such as Confidential, Restricted, For Official Use Only, or a named distribution list, alone; the caption is a literal observation, it does not prove authority-side custody, and it must never be promoted into a handling class
a country name, a country pair, or a two-letter country code alone; travel, trade, research, immigration, and photo material all carry them

a visa, residence permit, entry stamp, passport, emergency travel document, apostille, legalisation sticker, or consular certificate held by the person named on it; the recipient's copy of a document a post issued is the recipient's identity or immigration record
a scheduled appointment, fee receipt, or portal confirmation from an embassy or consulate held by an applicant; that is a service transaction, not the post's case
an international organisation, mission, or ministry name on a person's resume, contract, payslip, or calendar; diplomatic service as an employer or as an industry is not this template
a published country report, human-rights report, travel advice page, treaty text, or press release downloaded for reference; publication by a foreign ministry is not post-side custody
a file extension or source_type alone; the design says to “treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning”
a parent folder named Embassy, Consulate, Foreign Affairs, Diplomatic, Visa, or a country name alone
a shared download session or browser batch of consular-portal pages; “A session should never be treated as proof of topic”
dense OCR text or absent metadata as proof that an image is a consular-system screenshot; the design says the system “must not mistake the absence of EXIF for proof that an image is a screenshot”
a contact export naming diplomats, host officials, or wardens; contacts “should normally be privacy-protected rather than used to create folder proposals”

work_types: reporting despatch, political or economic report, spot report, scene-setter, or annual post review
note verbale, third-person note, demarche instruction, delivery report, aide-memoire, or readout
credentials, agrement, accreditation, privileges and immunities, or protocol register entry
treaty action, memorandum of understanding, exchange of letters, full powers, ratification instrument, or depositary notification
consular protection case, detention or arrest notification, welfare visit, hospitalisation, death abroad, or repatriation record
passport, citizenship, or emergency-travel-document service on the issuing side
visa or entry-permission application, interview record, adjudication, refusal reasons, or review
notarial act, legalisation, apostille, or consular report of birth, marriage, or death abroad
crisis and evacuation planning, warden network, travel-advice change, or incident log
public diplomacy, cultural or scholarship programme, press engagement, or national-day event record
commercial diplomacy, trade mission, market-access representation, or investment enquiry handling
post administration: estate, locally engaged staff, mission security, diplomatic bag, or consular fee accounting
registry transfer, retirement, or archive manifest produced by the post
grouping_reasons: one evidenced post drawer whose members are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent: reporting, protocol notes, consular acts, services registers, and post administration cohere because they were produced by one mission, not because they share a subject. The design makes this shape first class: “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
one reporting thread linked by an exact despatch, telegram, or post reference number across a draft, a cleared version, an addressed copy, and a capital acknowledgement
one note-verbale exchange linked by the outgoing note number and the incoming note number it quotes, including any enclosure named in the note

one consular protection case linked by an exact case reference, kept inside a protected, locally processed group; a national's name, nationality, host state, or detaining authority is never sufficient to join two cases
one instrument or negotiation linked by an exact instrument title plus session, round, or signature-ceremony reference, keeping delegation papers separate from the signed text
one crisis or incident bounded by an exact incident or activation reference; a shared host state or region is not a grouping anchor
one post export, registry transfer, or archive manifest kept shallow until access boundaries are known and never unpacked merely to strengthen recognition

duplicate and version families remain universal relationships; repeated drafts of a note, report, advice page, or instrument do not acquire post, case, or classification facts from their neighbourhood

no group is a valid outcome for a standalone civic or official document; “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

template.why: Empty by contract. PR-6 leaves the `government` schema fieldless, and a template may not branch on fields its schema has not declared. The world does have a recommendable shape, and it is recorded here as prose rather than serialized: the organizing dimension is the post itself (a sending-state authority at a named host-state location), then the post function or bounded thread (reporting thread, note exchange, protection case, services register, instrument, crisis activation), then work type. A named national, a named host official, or a named diplomat must never become an organizing dimension, because a visible branch label would disclose that a person is the subject of a consular protection case. Time is not first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” Any later order stays the user's: “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: The generic authority-side row and this one compete over exactly the same bytes for post administration, correspondence registers, meeting records, procurement, budget, and registry transfers. `Post registry transfer 2026 - retired consular files.zip` is the shared fixture. This template requires the post/sending-state/host-state triangle in the evidence: an origin post operating outside its own state, addressing a capital or a host-state ministry. Absent that triangle, an authority record with only a body name and internal governance shape stays with the generic authority record. Reciprocally, the generic row must not claim a note verbale, a consular protection case, or an issuance register merely because a public body produced it.

Both hold named-person case files opened by a public office, with case references, contact blocks, chase correspondence, and a protected posture. `Consular Protection Case CP-2026-0417 - detention notification and visit log.docx` is the shared fixture: strip the host-state detaining authority and it reads as ordinary casework. This template requires the national to be outside the sending state's territory with a host-state authority as counterparty and a post as case owner. Reciprocally, constituent casework keeps every case where the office and the person are inside the same jurisdiction, including immigration or passport enquiries handled by a domestic representative on a constituent's behalf.

Visas, residence permits, entry stamps, emergency travel documents, and consular civil-registration certificates exist on both sides of the same counter. The shared fixture is the visa: `Visa refusal - decision and reasons - case NIV-88213.pdf` on the post side against `My Schengen visa - approved 2026.jpg` on the holder side. This template requires issuing-side structure: a case or act number, an adjudicating or issuing officer, reasons, a register row, or a fee-taken slot. Reciprocally, immigration and visa records keep every finished document, appointment confirmation, application copy, and status letter held by the person named on it, and the presence of a consulate name never moves it here.

A mission frequently administers a bilateral cooperation or aid portfolio, so programme design, monitoring, evaluation, and partner-government correspondence appear on both sides. `Bilateral MOU on Education Cooperation - signed text and exchange of letters.pdf` is the shared fixture. This template keeps the representation and instrument side: the negotiating record, the exchange of letters, the note verbale conveying it, the reporting on it. Reciprocally, international development keeps the programme lifecycle once an evidenced portfolio, grant, or implementing-partner structure exists, even where the post is the administering unit.

Registry transfers, retention schedules, and manifests sit on both sides of the accession line. `Post registry transfer 2026 - retired consular files.zip` is the shared fixture. This template holds the transferring post's own schedule and covering correspondence up to the point of transfer. Reciprocally, archives and recordkeeping holds the record once accession, arrangement, description, catalogue identifiers, or access-review structure is evidenced on the receiving side.

International advocacy reproduces the diplomatic register exactly: session references, delegation lists, demarche-shaped asks, briefing packs, and multilateral agenda items. `UN side event - NGO delegation briefing and lobbying plan.pdf` is the shared fixture. This template requires an evidenced public authority producing or receiving the paper on a post's side. Reciprocally, advocacy campaign keeps the record whenever the producer block, registration details, or funding structure evidences a civil-society organisation, however governmental the vocabulary looks.

Trade-mission packs, market-entry briefings, and matchmaking schedules are produced by posts and by the companies that join them. `Trade mission to host market - participant pack and matchmaking schedule.pdf` is the shared fixture. This template requires post-side production: a post reference, an approval or reporting slot, or a commercial-section case. Reciprocally, go-to-market keeps a company's own copy of a trade-mission pack, and an embassy contact block on it changes nothing.

falls_through_to.when: a consular protection case, issuance register, adjudication file, protocol register, warden list, post payroll, or mixed post packet is recognized as sensitive but has no safe accepted group; also the destination for the holder's own visa, passport, or consular certificate when no other domain group is active
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

falls_through_to.when: a standalone readable official document — a single note verbale, a signed instrument, a fee reconciliation, a legalisation certificate, a public notice — has durable value but no post-side workflow and no accepted neighbouring group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.when: a published country report, travel-advice page, treaty text, foreign-policy paper, or press release is held for reading rather than as post-side work
falls_through_to.design_cite: Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.

falls_through_to.when: the document is plainly official or international in register but the holder role is unresolved — post, ministry desk, advocacy organisation, participating company, researcher, or applicant cannot be separated from the evidence available locally
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.when: a case-system export, encrypted registry container, damaged transfer, or unknown binary cannot be read, and its filename must not manufacture a post, case, or sensitivity result
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.when: an isolated consular appointment confirmation, fee receipt, or courier booking held by an applicant or by the post has no accepted case or administrative group
falls_through_to.design_cite: Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.

sensitivity_why: The post drawer routinely contains named nationals in adverse circumstances abroad — detention, hospitalisation, death, destitution, evacuation — together with next-of-kin contacts, identity and travel-document serials, visa adjudication reasoning, warden home addresses, locally engaged staff pay and host-state tax data, protocol registers naming diplomats and dependants, and pre-decisional reporting. The extraterritorial setting sharpens this: the persons named are inside a jurisdiction that is not the sending state's, so exposure can have consequences the product cannot foresee or measure. The design requires: “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.” Handling captions and distribution markings found in these files are literal source observations only; this phase records `potentially_sensitive` and nothing else, and P7 owns handling classes. Published ministry reports and signed public instruments can be low-risk bytes on their own, but their presence inside a post packet cannot lower the packet's posture.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: three unsettled items. (1) Whether the sending-state / host-state / post triangle is representable at all once PR-6 is revisited, or whether every post concept stays prose; if representable, whether a post identifier could ever be destination-eligible given that a country-named branch can itself disclose a person's location or case. (2) Whether the post-side issuance and adjudication records (visa, passport, emergency travel document, civil registration abroad) belong to this template or reciprocally to `government.permit-licensing` as the general decision-making row; this row currently claims them on the extraterritorial-post argument and the alternative is a clean function-first split that would leave this row holding only reporting, protocol, and protection. (3) Whether handling captions and distribution markings may ever be retained as literal observations for local review, or must be dropped at extraction so they can never be mistaken for a sensitivity vocabulary.
